derivation.method: Import the kit FBX with Blender (file axes and FBX_SCALE_UNITS honoured: metres, Z-up); remove engine collision hulls (UCX_*) and apply the recorded edits (source_edits); remove the kit material slots (Almond materials are assigned; kit textures are not shipped); Validate mesh; weld coincident vertices; dissolve degenerates; recalculate normals; collapse decimation only when above target with validation between passes; triangulate and validate before measuring. Remove wire edges, split edges shared by more than two faces and remove zero-area faces (counts in quality.topology_repairs). Mark edges sharper than 30 degrees as sharp (flat-shaded hard edges; shading only). Never subdivide to inflate counts.

quality.use: Visual entourage; not certified for fabrication or structural analysis

external_reference_status: Style reference only: kit_v040.py says it builds "in the style of the owner's Ginkgo refset_0924 world run" (the owner's own generated world images); kit_v060_details.py and kinetic_v046.py follow the owner's text requests. No external image was an input to these pieces, and the pieces use no Ginkgo or Meshy geometry (the shrine, railcars and street details are built from boxes, cylinders and struts).
dimension_basis: Authored kit sizes in metres from the scripts (kit records: kit_v060.json min/max, kit_v040.json bounds_m); the library keeps them (height = authored height, width and depth measured). The wall AC rig is assumed to hang with its drain line reaching ground level (mount height 0). Not a physical survey.
reference_review: Reviewed on 2026-11-20: procedural geometry, so there is no input image. The prepared library mesh was rendered untextured from the front three-quarter view (500 px, viewed in a 300 px contact sheet) and the script code that models it was read: no lettering, logos, brand marks or characters in the geometry. The livery is plain material slots. A generic commuter car, not a specific operator's rolling stock.
rights: Procedural geometry built by a Blender script in the owner's Project Y2K game repository (private); see each script's authoring record for the Claude Code session that wrote it, or that none was found. The owner's own project geometry: no generation provider, account or credits are involved, and the scripts build every piece from Blender primitives (no imported or third-party geometry in these pieces). Owner approved release in the Almond library under CC BY 4.0 on 2026-11-20 ("increase the range of models, from the ones i used for my project y2k games, (except for the operatives and bosses)") and chose the procedural kit pieces on 2026-11-20. Kit material colours and textures are not distributed; Almond materials are assigned.
